# FunMel

**From fungal confrontation photographs to matched-control results.**

FunMel measures the colour, shape and melanization index of
approximately round *Zymoseptoria tritici* colonies surrounding another
fungus. It separates central fungal tissue and hyphal growth from the
target colonies. The outlines can be irregular; photographs do not
establish species identity.

Melanization index (MI) is `100 - CIELAB L*`. Larger values mean darker
tissue. This is an image-darkness proxy, not a direct measurement of
melanin concentration.

## Install

``` r

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel")
library(FunMel)
```

Restart R before updating a loaded package. R \>= 4.1 and a compilation
toolchain are required: Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, matching
Rtools on Windows, or R development tools and ImageMagick development
libraries on Linux. To install the local vignette:

``` r

remotes::install_github("mghotbi/FunMel", build_vignettes = TRUE,
                        dependencies = TRUE)
vignette("FunMel", package = "FunMel")
```

## Start here: prepare, run, finish

**No approval columns need to be edited.** FunMel prints review
reminders and proceeds automatically with valid metadata. Check
experimental assignments before processing and inspect image QC before
interpreting results. Missing labels, unmatched controls and failed
images still need correction.

### 1. Prepare a photograph folder or ZIP

``` r

project <- prepare_experiment(file.choose(), "FunMel_project")
# Select a ZIP, or replace file.choose() with a photograph-folder path.
project$metadata_file
```

Use a new project folder. The ZIP may contain nested batches and
repeated image basenames; relative paths distinguish files. With folders
such as `batch_1/control/`, `batch_1/fungus_A/`, `batch_2/control/` and
`batch_2/fungus_B/`, the package proposes matching sets and treatment
labels. Only explicit `control` or `controls` folders denote controls by
default. Use `control_folders="C"` only if that label really means
control. A unique `plate_metadata.csv` inside the input is read
automatically; alternatively supply one combined table through
`metadata=`. Ambiguous file names do not establish biological
assignments.

Review the printed metadata file. **Only correct missing or inaccurate
information; there is no confirmation switch.** One row represents one
independent plate.

| Column | Meaning |
|----|----|
| `file`, `relative_file`, `plate_id` | Photograph provenance and unique plate identity; preserve these |
| `set_id` | Treatment plates and their own relevant control plates |
| `treatment` | `control` or the actual treatment name |
| `centre_model` | `none` for a control; `fungus` for a central fungus |
| `partner_type` | Biological partner, normally `none` or `fungus` |
| `day`, `medium`, `zymo_strain` | Recorded context; complete and constant within each matching set |
| `replicate`, `fungus`, `photo_date`, `notes` | Experimental annotations |

For one control and three treatment plates, use four rows sharing a
`set_id`. Enter the control once. Four colonies and any sampling spots
on a plate are subsamples, not independent biological replicates.
Repeated photographs of the same plate are repeated observations, not
additional independent plates.

### 2. Run image analysis

``` r

dish_mm <- 90  # Replace with the verified outer dish diameter (mm).
result <- run_experiment(project, dish_diameter_mm = dish_mm,
                         n_spots = 5, spot_radius_mm = 0.4)
result$analysis_status
result$failed
```

The diameter is a numeric value, not an interactive prompt. Omit
`n_spots` and `spot_radius_mm` for whole-colony measurements alone.
Spots are additional, deterministically distributed, non-overlapping
circular ROIs inside eligible colony tissue. Five spots are requested
per colony in this example; they are not five independent replicates.
Choose settings consistently across plates. If spots cannot fit,
`spot_status="insufficient_space"`; achieved ROIs remain available, but
the requested spot summary is unavailable.

Inspect the QC PNGs in `project$qc_dir`: target masks, central fungal
tissue and hyphae, spot outlines, scale, shadows, illumination and
warnings. Correct measurement problems before interpretation.
Informative reminders do not require approval-flag edits. Any failed
photographs must be resolved before finalization.

### 3. Finish and export

``` r

reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)
reviewed$melanization_coefficient
```

This reads the saved measurements and metadata and exports tables, an
assessment RDS and a comparison figure in PDF, SVG and 600-dpi PNG. It
does not reprocess photographs or require manual approval. Unconfirmed
image QC warns and remains recorded; it does not block the default
workflow or automatically approve plates. Different recorded days,
strains and media are reported separately in context folders; consult
`context_index.csv` when present.

## Understand the outputs

The coefficient is
`mean(treatment plate MI) / mean(matching control plate MI)`. A plate’s
MI is the equally weighted mean of its target-colony `MI_mean` values.
Each treatment uses only controls in its own set. Values above 1
indicate a darker treatment mean, not a fold increase in melanin
concentration.

`colonies.csv` contains whole-colony `MI_min`, `MI_mean` and `MI_max`
for eligible interior pixels. `spots.csv` contains individual ROI
measurements. `MI_spot_mean/min/max` summarize the individual **spot
means**, not pixel extrema or confidence limits. Default coefficients
use whole-colony MI. A prespecified spot-based descriptive analysis can
use:

``` r

spot_coefficients <- melanization_coefficient(reviewed, response = "MI_spot_mean")
```

Keep spot and whole-colony results labelled separately. Independent
plates are the biological units. One control per set permits descriptive
ratios but does not meet the built-in replicated-cell inference guard.
Supported mixed-model assessment uses `lme4`/`lmerTest`, plate-level
random effects and matched-set contrasts. Check design, residuals,
convergence and singularity before using p-values. The comparison figure
shows between-plate SD, not confidence intervals; ratio SD does not
include uncertainty in a shared control mean.

## Follow eight real photographs

The vignette and `examples/walkthrough_14_days.R` use eight original
photographs: A60_2 and B20_2, each with one control and three
confrontation plates. No separate download is required. The combined
metadata is supplied, so the example runs without approval-column
editing. Verify labels against laboratory records and use the actual
dish diameter for scientific interpretation.

``` r

vignette("FunMel", package = "FunMel")
```

The original JPEGs are unchanged. Precomputed tables are illustrative
results with a 90-mm scale, `max_dim=1200`, five 0.4-mm-radius spots and
`n_boot=20`; see `extdata/14_day_example/PROVENANCE.md`. They are not
biological ground truth.

## Try one simulated image

``` r

sim <- simulate_plate(width = 400, height = 400, seed = 1)
x <- analyze_plate(sim$image, n_spots = 3, spot_radius_mm = 0.4,
                   n_boot = 20, verbose = FALSE)
plot_qc(x)
x$colonies[, c("colony_id", "MI_min", "MI_mean", "MI_max", "MI_spot_mean")]
```

For a control, use `layout=plate_layout(centre="none")`. Advanced
functions
[`analyze_plate()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/analyze_plate.md),
[`analyze_plates()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/analyze_plates.md),
[`make_metadata()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/make_metadata.md),
[`prepare_photo_archive()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/prepare_photo_archive.md)
and
[`finalize_analysis()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/finalize_analysis.md)
remain available.

## Metadata, calibration and recovery

Additional metadata columns retain their names and values. The complete
table is exported as `metadata_used.csv`. A collision with a measured
column receives a `metadata_` prefix in measurement tables; original
names remain in the full metadata. An optional recorded `qc_pass` field
starts FALSE and is reset for a new image run, but never needs editing
for default calculations.

Entirely unrecorded day/strain/medium columns may remain blank. Once
recorded, complete them for all plates and keep each context constant
within a set. Do not hide differing experimental contexts to pool
incompatible plates.

`flat_field=TRUE` requests spatial illumination correction. It can be
withheld when fitted gains saturate: inspect `flat_field_applied`,
`flat_field_status` and warnings in `plates.csv`. Withholding does not
establish adequate lighting; matched ratios do not guarantee
cancellation of illumination bias.

Resume an existing project without recreating it:

``` r

project <- readRDS(file.choose()) # Select the existing project.rds.
reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)
```

Printing a stored path does not prove that the file exists. Restore
missing metadata from the saved edited CSV, or point
`project$metadata_file` to that existing file and save the updated
project object. Download cloud files locally. Use `result$failed` to
resolve image errors. The package never invents missing experimental
assignments. Reanalysis is necessary if image-layout settings change.

The separate [algorithm
overview](https://github.com/mghotbi/FunMel/blob/HEAD/inst/guides/FunMel_overview.md)
describes the methods and comparison with ImageJ/Fiji. Manual ROI tools
remain useful for difficult boundaries; no universal accuracy or speed
superiority is claimed.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`analyze_plate()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/analyze_plate.md)
  : Analyse one plate photograph

- [`analyze_plates()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/analyze_plates.md)
  : Analyse many plates

- [`annotate_plate()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/annotate_plate.md)
  : Interactively annotate training regions

- [`assess_experiment()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/assess_experiment.md)
  : Assess matched treatment effects within and across control sets

- [`calibrate_color()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/calibrate_color.md)
  : Colour / exposure calibration against a reference patch

- [`classify_pixels()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/classify_pixels.md)
  : Classify target colonies and central fungal growth

- [`colony_profiles()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/colony_profiles.md)
  : Edge-to-centre melanization profiles

- [`compare_melanization()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/compare_melanization.md)
  : Compare colony measurements while accounting for plates

- [`correct_facing_bias()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/correct_facing_bias.md)
  : Remove position-specific lighting bias from side-specific metrics

- [`delta_e76()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/delta_e76.md)
  :

  Colour difference CIE76 (Euclidean distance in L*a*b\*)

- [`detect_plate()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/detect_plate.md)
  : Detect the Petri dish and set the spatial scale

- [`example_experiment()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/example_experiment.md)
  : Reproducible synthetic matched-set experiment for learning the
  workflow

- [`example_plate()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/example_plate.md)
  : Paths to the example plate photographs shipped with FunMel

- [`extract_training_pixels()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/extract_training_pixels.md)
  : Extract annotated training pixels

- [`finalize_analysis()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/finalize_analysis.md)
  : Finalize saved measurements after reviewing metadata and image masks

- [`finish_experiment()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/finish_experiment.md)
  : Finalize a prepared experiment after plate review

- [`is_funmel_plate()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/is_funmel_plate.md)
  : Test for a FunMel plate object

- [`is_mycohalo_plate()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/is_mycohalo_plate.md)
  : Check a plate object (compatibility name from MycoHalo)

- [`lab_chroma_hue()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/lab_chroma_hue.md)
  : Chroma and hue angle from a\* and b\*

- [`lab_to_srgb()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/lab_to_srgb.md)
  :

  Convert CIE L*a*b\* to sRGB

- [`layout_by_treatment()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/layout_by_treatment.md)
  : Choose a segmentation layout from one metadata row

- [`make_metadata()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/make_metadata.md)
  : Create a metadata template for matched treatment-control sets

- [`measure_colonies()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/measure_colonies.md)
  : Measure colonies: size, shape, melanization and interaction metrics

- [`melanization_coefficient()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/melanization_coefficient.md)
  : Calculate the treatment-to-control melanization coefficient

- [`model_background()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/model_background.md)
  : Model the agar background and correct uneven illumination

- [`plate_layout()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/plate_layout.md)
  : Describe the inoculation layout of a plate

- [`plot_melanization_map()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/plot_melanization_map.md)
  : Melanization landscape: 3D shaded surface and 2D map of a plate

- [`plot_profiles()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/plot_profiles.md)
  : Plot edge-to-centre melanization profiles

- [`plot_qc()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/plot_qc.md) :
  Quality-control figure

- [`plot_treatment_comparison()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/plot_treatment_comparison.md)
  : Plot plate-level darkness and matched melanization coefficients

- [`prepare_experiment()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/prepare_experiment.md)
  : Prepare a folder or ZIP as a reviewable experiment project

- [`prepare_photo_archive()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/prepare_photo_archive.md)
  : Extract and locate the photographs required by metadata

- [`print(`*`<funmel_result>`*`)`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/print_funmel.md)
  [`print(`*`<funmel_classifier>`*`)`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/print_funmel.md)
  [`print(`*`<funmel_layout>`*`)`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/print_funmel.md)
  [`print(`*`<funmel_plate>`*`)`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/print_funmel.md)
  : Print a FunMel object summary

- [`read_plate()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/read_plate.md)
  : Read a plate photograph

- [`run_experiment()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/run_experiment.md)
  : Analyze all photographs in a prepared experiment

- [`sample_colony_spots()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/sample_colony_spots.md)
  : Sample a chosen number of circular spots within each target colony

- [`segment_colonies()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/segment_colonies.md)
  : Separate Zymoseptoria targets and the central fungal colony

- [`simulate_plate()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/simulate_plate.md)
  : Simulate a plate photograph with known ground truth

- [`srgb_to_lab()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/srgb_to_lab.md)
  :

  Convert sRGB values to CIE 1976 L*a*b\*

- [`train_classifier()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/train_classifier.md)
  : Train a supervised pixel classifier

- [`validate_metadata()`](https://mghotbi.github.io/FunMel/reference/validate_metadata.md)
  : Validate the plate-to-set metadata used for matched controls
